meta.title: Operation of Tapped Density Apparatus in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the tapped density and Carr's Index (compressibility index) of powdered crude drugs to assess powder flow characteristics and predict behavior during encapsulation or tableting.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for standardization of powdered crude drugs as per Indian Pharmacopoeia (IP) and WHO guidelines on crude drug quality assessment.
procedure: Ensure the tapped density apparatus is clean, dry, and properly calibrated.
Weigh the empty graduated measuring cylinder (100 mL) and record the weight (W₁).
Pass the drug powder through a 1000 µm (No. 18) sieve to break agglomerates without compressing the powder.
Carefully pour the sieved powder into the graduated measuring cylinder without compacting — fill to approximately 100 mL or as per method.
Level the powder surface gently with a spatula — avoid pressing down.
Record the initial volume (V₀) — this is used to calculate bulk density: Bulk density = Mass / V₀.
Place the cylinder on the tapped density apparatus and set the number of taps to 500 (or as per the method: IP recommends 100, 500, 1250 taps).
Start the machine — it will mechanically tap the cylinder at a fixed rate (typically 250 ± 15 taps per minute, 14 ± 2 mm drop height).
Continue tapping to 1250 taps and record the volume (V₁₂₅₀).
If the difference between V₅₀₀ and V₁₂₅₀ is less than 2 mL, use V₅₀₀ as the tapped volume (Vₜ).
If the difference is greater than 2 mL, continue tapping in increments of 1250 taps until constant volume is achieved.
Weigh the cylinder with powder (W₂); calculate mass of powder = W₂ − W₁.
Calculate: Tapped density = Mass / Vₜ; Carr's Index (%) = [(Vₜ − V₀) / Vₜ] × 100.
Interpret Carr's Index: <15% = excellent flow; 15–25% = acceptable; >35% = very poor flow.
Record all values in the practical register with drug name, batch, and calculated indices.
precautions: Do not compress or compact the powder during filling — this artificially inflates bulk density.
Ensure the cylinder is clean and dry before each determination — residual moisture or previous drug residue alters results.
Check the drop height (14 ± 2 mm) and tap rate (250 ± 15 taps/min) as per apparatus specification.
Calibrate the tapped density apparatus regularly using standard reference powder (e.g., microcrystalline cellulose).
Allow the cylinder to cool to room temperature if used previously for a different run.
Use the same cylinder throughout the experiment — different cylinders have different weights and calibrations.
Wear a dust mask when working with fine powders.
